text:
samir: p99 latency spike observed on gpu-pool-east-1 around 11:12 UTC. throughput down ~25% for short-seq workloads.
infra-bot: incident INC-2025-213 created and linked to #incidents. severity: high.
katie: grabbing profiles now, looks like kernel selector churn + KV cache evictions. posting profiler snippet:
``` 
kernel_selector: pickScore(v1)=0.42 -> pickScore(v2)=0.58 at 11:12:03
kvcache.evictions: 4203 events over 18s
batcher.window_ms: 0.7 -> 3.1 (backpressure)
worker.cpu.spin: +12%
``` 
lee: noted. aggressive_shortseq_merge heuristic appears to be merging 8-16 token requests into long-kernel paths. that causes big kernels + warmups.
maria: proposing immediate mitigations: 1) disable aggressive_shortseq_merge in east pool, 2) enable routing fallback to redwood-small-quant for non-critical tenants, 3) pin KV for hot tenants (tenant-42/tenant-77).
samir: I'll apply a soft throttle to tenant-42 to protect KV cache: `/throttle tenant-42 30% --reason=kv-evictions` :hourglass:
lee: command to flip flag:
`fftool set aggressive_shortseq_merge false --env=prod --scope=gpu-pool-east-1 --no-wait`
deploy-bot: rollout started for featureflag aggressive_shortseq_merge=false in gpu-pool-east-1 (canary 10%)
infra-bot: monitoring alert channel update every 30s, dashboard: https://perf.redwood/boards/INC-2025-213
oncall: ack, please post rollback steps and ETA. also keep an eye on kernel-selector logs for flapping.
katie: rollback plan — re-enable flag and revert routing: `fftool set aggressive_shortseq_merge true` + `route set default model=redwood-llm-v2` . ETA <10m if needed.
maria: after throttle + flag flip, KV evictions dropped 78% in next sample, p99 improving. leaving routing fallback on until morning.
samir: tagging incident doc https://docs.redwood/incidents/INC-2025-213 with steps and timeline. will update every 15m. :thumbsup:
oncall: thanks all, keep updates short. if p99 stays >500ms we'll escalate to infra pager.
